hook: A Roman Emperor Who Hated Getting Out of Bed
text: Almost two thousand years ago, in a freezing army camp beside the river Danube, the emperor Marcus Aurelius wrote a little note to himself. In the morning, he wrote, when you rise unwillingly, let this thought be present. I am rising to the work of a human being. Then he argued with himself, very gently. Or have I been made for this, he asked, to lie in the bedclothes and keep myself warm? The most powerful man in the world had the same argument with his blankets that we all have on a cold morning. He wrote it down, and kept on writing, by lamplight, night after night.
